item.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore enhances AI agent evaluation with new metrics and custom tools
item.description:
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore enhances AI agent evaluation with new metrics and custom tools

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore has introduced expanded evaluation capabilities for AI agents, combining built-in, third-party, and customizable metrics to assess performance across multiple dimensions. This update provides developers with a comprehensive toolkit to measure agent effectiveness at both granular and conversational levels.

🔍 Overview

AgentCore now integrates three evaluator types: AWS-authored built-in evaluators, third-party managed evaluators from DeepEval/AutoEval, and custom derivations. These tools assess agent behaviors through:

  • Trace-level metrics: Per-turn or per-tool-call analysis
  • Session-level metrics: Holistic conversation outcomes

🧩 How it works

  • Built-in evaluators (e.g., Builtin.GoalSuccessRate, Builtin.Helpfulness) are pre-configured by AWS and referenced by ID.
  • Third-party managed evaluators leverage DeepEval/AutoEval libraries, with AgentCore handling hosting and inference.
  • Custom evaluators modify existing evaluators’ models, prompts, or rubrics while retaining standard usage.

⚙️ Key details

The system covers 18+ evaluation dimensions across five categories:

Category Evaluators
Task Completion GoalSuccessRate, ToolSelectionAccuracy, ToolParameterAccuracy
Skills SkillSelectionAccuracy, SkillInstructionFollowing
Safety Harmfulness, Stereotyping, Security
Conversation ConversationCompleteness, KnowledgeRetention, Possible
Trajectory TrajectoryExactOrderMatch, TrajectoryInOrderMatch, TrajectoryAnyOrderMatch

Additional specialized metrics include Humor for consumer agents.

💡 Why it matters

  • Reliability: Built-in evaluators are AWS-benchmarked for common use cases.
  • Flexibility: Third-party integration allows reuse of existing development metrics in production.
  • Customization: Developers can create domain-specific evaluators without starting from scratch.
  • Comprehensive coverage: Metrics span tool accuracy, safety, long-term context retention, and conversational flow.

#AIagents #AmazonBedrock #EvaluationTools #LLM #AutoEval #DeepEval

Source: The agent evaluation playbook: Built-in, DeepEval, and AutoEval on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations | Amazon Web Services

item.title: SkillEval: Cross-model Skill-Level Assessment Framework for LLMs
item.description:
SkillEval: Cross-model Skill-Level Assessment Framework for LLMs

We propose SkillEval, a new evaluation framework that performs cross‑model, skill‑level analysis.

🔍 Overview

SkillEval is designed to move beyond average‑based scoring by producing reliable, calibrated, and concise profiles of language models.

🧩 How it works

  • Meta‑cognitive skill discovery – the framework leverages the meta‑cognitive capabilities of LLMs to automatically uncover interpretable skills from questions.
  • Cognitive Diagnosis Models (CDMs) – it applies CDMs from psychometrics to estimate per‑skill abilities for each LLM.

📊 Experiments

  • Evaluated 3,811 LLMs on 9,523 items.
  • Benchmarks covered: MATH, BBH, GPQA, MuSR, IFEval (five diverse domains).
  • Compared with the traditional average‑based evaluation paradigm, SkillEval’s profiles more accurately predict model behavior on unseen items.

🚀 Benefits & Applications

  • More calibrated and informative model profiles while remaining concise.
  • Downstream task 1 – LLM routing: dynamically routes each query to a capable but efficient model, reducing inference cost by over 60% and improving performance.
  • Downstream task 2 – Computerized Adaptive Testing (CAT): an unseen model can be efficiently evaluated using a trained CDM.
  • Insight generation: skill profiles reveal how benchmarks share skills and illustrate differences between instruction‑tuned models and their base counterparts.

#SkillEval #LLMEvaluation #AIProfiling

Source: SkillEval: Learning Interpretable Ability Profiles of LLMs via Cognitive Diagnosis Models Source: Our Own Jev: Typed Decisions in One Forward Pass, from an In-House Judge to Open LoRA Models
